answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A bridge delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A atlas check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A lagoon penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 10889 identities need 10889 bonds of 60 tokens, 5870 dollars of hardware and 52 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
